While Tayba Foundation serves incarcerated individuals, their programs focus primarily on education, life skills, and re-entry support, which align more closely with Fi Sabilillah (educational/religious causes) or Fuqara/Masakin (if providing direct financial aid for basic needs upon release).

rich_narrative.summary: Tayba Foundation provides distance learning, higher education, and re-entry support to incarcerated individuals across the United States. In FY2025 filings, the organization reported <cite id="3">$1,460,391 in total revenue</cite> alongside an overall <cite id="1">Charity Navigator score of 94.2/100</cite>. Operating in a specialized niche within domestic poverty alleviation, Tayba delivers structured academic and character-building courses designed to support long-term rehabilitation. Revenue experienced a recent drop, shifting from <cite id="3">$1,460,391 in FY2023</cite> to <cite id="3">$1,263,096 in FY2024</cite>. The organization holds <cite id="1">a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite> and maintains <cite id="1">6.7 months of working capital</cite> to ensure operational resilience. Tayba Foundation is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite>, maintaining an explicit policy for distributing funds to eligible beneficiaries such as the poor and those seeking freedom.
